response: Yes, research suggests a potential relationship between homocysteine and vitiligo. Elevated homocysteine levels have been found in some patients with vitiligo, a chronic skin condition characterized by the loss of pigment-producing cells (melanocytes). High homocysteine levels may contribute to oxidative stress and inflammation, which could potentially exacerbate vitiligo. However, more studies are needed to fully understand the relationship between homocysteine and vitiligo.
